text:
Sam T: Thinking out loud: our postmortem actions are scattered across docs and tickets. Proposal: create a lightweight 'incident remediation board' (Kanban) and a 2-week timebox for quick remediations. Keep ownership + recurrence tags on each card.

Priya K: Agree. We need clear metadata on each card: owner (primary+backup), ETA, verification steps, blocking-deps, recurrence_count, SLA impact.

Sam T: Exactly. Minimal fields so updating is low friction. Card example:
```
Title: Fix hot-path cache miss on model load (INC-123)
Owner: Priya K (primary), Omar B (backup)
Priority: P1
ETA: 2026-04-06
Verification: load test < 150ms p95, no error spike for 48h
Blocking: infra upgrade v2.1 (owner: Eng-Infra)
Recurrence: 2 in last 6mo
2w-sprint?: yes
```

Omar B: I like the recurrence field. Also propose a small taxonomy for root cause tags: config, infra, model, deploy, third-party. That will let monthly trend queries.

Jess L: For IC rotation, suggestion: pair ICs for a 2-week handoff window. Primary IC leads the first week and documents decisions; backup does the second week and closes any follow-ups. Rotation schedule posted in the playbook.

Priya K: Operational note: every card in the 2-week lane must have a short verification checklist and a monitoring query attached (link to metric or dashboard). Otherwise "done" is fuzzy.

Sam T: Good. Also add a small comms template on the card for stakeholder updates: one-line status + risk + ETA + contact.

Omar B: Automation idea: when a postmortem mentions a remediation, create a board card via a template. Minimal manual work. We can start with a Google Sheet + Zapier if we need quick rollout, then migrate to Jira/Asana board.

Jess L: We should limit what goes into the 2-week board: only actions that unblock reliability quickly. Larger work should be escalated to roadmap with a PM owner.

incident-bot: Reminder created: #eng-oncall 2w-remediation-check Tue 10:00 recurring starting 1823157600

Sam T: Proposed cadence:
- D0 incident: capture immediate actions in channel + create board card for any short remediation
- D1 postmortem draft + auto-create cards for named remediations
- Weekly (Tue 10:00): 15-min board sync for open 2-week items
- End of 2w: review, close verified items, escalate long items to roadmap with PM owner

Priya K: Can we add a quick field for "rollback window" and "blast radius"? Helps prioritize rollout strategy.

Omar B: Yep. Also add "monitoring duration" (how long we'll observe after change). Default 48h, allow override.

Jess L: Volunteers: I'll set up the initial board (Google Sheets prototype) and add the template fields. Priya, can you draft the verification checklist snippet?

Priya K: I can do the verification checklist. Will post in #eng-oncall within 3 days.

Sam T: Actions:
- Jess L: create prototype board + template (due in 3 days)
- Priya K: verification checklist + comms snippet (due in 3 days)
- Omar B: draft small automation sketch for card creation (due in 1 week)
- Sam T: update incident playbook with board flow and IC rotation notes (due in 1 week)

Priya K: One more ask: let's include a monthly incident trends review to look at recurrence tags and policy gaps. Could be 30-min monthly.

Sam T: Agreed. Add monthly trends review to ops calendar.

Jess L: I'll drop the sheet link and examples once ready.

Priya K: +1 to the approach. Low friction, measurable outcomes.

Omar B: +1. If the prototype works we can move to a proper board and hook into alerts.

Sam T: Thanks team. If no objections I'll add these tasks to the playbook and ping when prototypes are up.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: monthly-incident-trends recurs starting 1825760000

Jess L: Done, sheet link posted: https://example.com/sheet (will replace with internal link)

Priya K: Thanks, looking forward to piloting this on the next incident.

Sam T: Closing the thread for now. We'll review pilots in 3 weeks.
